findings.source_locator: opening of second paragraph: 'So fare thee well, poor devil of a Sub-Sub, whose commentator I am.'
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'whose commentator I am' is the moment the narrator identifies himself in relation to the Sub-Sub — a meta-textual, voice-establishing aside critical to understanding the framing device. Its removal erases the narrator's self-positioning.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'whose commentator I am' in the farewell sentence: 'So fare thee well, poor devil of a Sub-Sub, whose commentator I am.'

findings.source_passage: Would that I could clear out Hampton Court and the Tuileries for ye! But gulp down your tears and hie aloft to the royal-mast with your hearts
findings.source_locator: Second paragraph, after 'For by how much the more pains ye take…go thankless!'
findings.why_it_matters: The Hampton Court/Tuileries exclamation and the 'gulp down your tears and hie aloft to the royal-mast' image are the rhetorical climax of the passage — tonally and prosodically distinctive, blending mock-heroic sympathy with nautical register. Their absence deflates the entire peroration.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore from 'Would that I could clear out Hampton Court…' through '…making refugees of long-pampered Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael, against your coming' and the closing antithesis about splintered/unsplinterable glasses, or at minimum the 'gulp down your tears and hie aloft' sentence.

findings.source_passage: your friends who have gone before are clearing out the seven-storied heavens, and making refugees of long-pampered Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael, against your coming. Here ye strike but splintered hearts together—there, ye shall strike unsplinterable glasses!
findings.source_locator: Final sentences of the second paragraph
findings.why_it_matters: The closing antithesis ('splintered hearts / unsplinterable glasses') is the rhetorical and tonal capstone of the Extracts preface — widely noted by critics as exemplifying Melville's mock-heroic, tragicomic register. Its complete absence removes the climactic signature moment of the segment.
findings.suggested_fix: The closing two sentences must be restored verbatim or near-verbatim; they are the highest-density signature prose in this segment.

findings.source_passage: Therefore you must not, in every case at least, take the higgledy-piggledy whale statements, however authentic, in these extracts, for veritable gospel cetology.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Higgledy-piggledy whale statements' and 'veritable gospel cetology' are tonally distinctive coinages that signal the narrator's ironic, playful erudition; their omission slightly flattens the opening paragraph's voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider restoring the 'higgledy-piggledy' disclaimer sentence to preserve the ironic framing of the extracts' reliability.

summary: Three medium-severity failures — erasure of the narrator's self-identification, loss of the Hampton Court/royal-mast exclamation, and complete absence of the signature 'splintered hearts / unsplinterable glasses' closing antithesis — strip the segment of its rhetorical climax and voice-establishing capstone, triggering regeneration.
